title: Triplets T (T3 + FIR7, M = 15): pruning the ready coefficients without refitting
question: How many of the 368 triplet terms of the ready closed-form model T (M = 15) with the smallest coefficients can be set to zero without refitting, while the BER reduction drops by at most 0.5 p.p.?
model: y_k = x_k + sum_{m <= n, |m|,|n|,|m+n| <= 15} C_mn x_{k+m} x_{k+n} x*_{k+m+n} + FIR7 (triplets.py, T3); window-31 centres, zeros outside the file
coefficients: experiments/E035_triplet_hybrid/results/warm_M15.npz: ridge closed form on all 30 train files, lambda 1e-4 chosen by validation BER from [1e-8, 1e-6, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1] (warm_info.json); no refit here
pruning: keep the K terms with the largest score, the others C = 0, kept C unchanged; FIR7 always kept; scores: abs = |C_mn|, abs_rms = |C_mn| * rms(T_mn) on the 30 train files; K = 368, 360, ..., 8, 0
seeds: none (deterministic, no training); one coefficient set (all 30 train files), no bootstrap replicas
control: not run: no training; the full set (K = 368) must reproduce the closed-form T3 M15 numbers of E039/E035
rule_draft: For each score: K_val = the smallest K with validation reduction >= validation reduction of the full set - 0.5 p.p.; the number of removable terms is 368 - K_val; test is reported at K_val (test drop vs the full set). The smallest K with test drop <= 0.5 p.p. is reported for information only and is not used for any choice. The score with the smaller K_val is called better only if the two K_val differ by >= 16 terms (two grid steps).
